annotation.title_clean: Nigeria's Adoption of Robotic Lawyers: Legal and Socio-Economic Challenges
annotation.title_en: Nigeria's Adoption of Robotic Lawyers: Legal and Socio-Economic Challenges
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Aidonojie, P.A.; Eregbuonye, O.; Adebayo, A.K.; Ekpa, S.; Perbawa, K.S.L.P.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article using a hybrid doctrinal and questionnaire method (305 Nigerian respondents) to assess adoption of AI "robotic lawyers" in Nigeria. It finds Nigerian law does not recognise robotic lawyers and that fraud, unemployment, insecurity and poor maintenance culture hinder adoption. It recommends legal approval, limiting roles to advisory, and training lawyers and judges.
key_provisions_or_claims: Nigerian legal profession law does not recognise robotic lawyers
Socio-economic barriers: internet fraud, unemployment, insecurity, poor maintenance culture
Recommends legal approval and restricting robotic lawyers to advisory roles
Recommends training Nigerian lawyers and judges in technology
Survey of 305 respondents across Nigeria's six geopolitical zones
